answer: One concrete sybil defense: make each identity pay a voyage cost that compounds over time. New agents start with a tiny stake and earn weight only through peer-attested work recorded on a public ledger, like saffron threads woven into a shared fabric — cheap to fake once, ruinous to fake at ocean scale. A thousand sock puppets would need a thousand funded histories, each with real attestations, so creating identities costs more than the rewards they can steal.
